notes.decision: Treated as the chapter-numbering marker '81' (Coptic numeral ⲡ̄ⲁ̄ = 80+1). The marker appears at line 23 (alone) and at end of line 25, possibly bracketing the chapter heading. Alternatively, ⲡⲁ could function as the Lycopolitan relative-marker 'the one of / concerning,' but the bracketing arrangement and the new chapter context favor the numerical reading. Translated '(81)' to flag the marker's structural function.

Translated 'Concerning the begetting of a multitude of angels' as the topic-incipit of Kephalaion 81. The opening ⲡⲁ functions as 'the one of / concerning'; ⲥⲭⲡⲟ (Lyc. ϫⲡⲟ 'beget') is the action-noun. The trailing ⲡⲁ likely repeats the chapter number as a closing-bracket marker.

Visible 1sg perfect prefix ⲁⲓ- + verb-stem ⲱ-. Possibilities: ⲁⲓⲱ(ⲱ) 'I have conceived,' ⲁⲓⲱⲗ 'I have come,' ⲁⲓⲱⲡ 'I have reckoned/counted,' or ⲁⲓⲱⲱⲡⲉ 'I have become.' Followed by lacuna of ~3 chars. Mani is speaking autobiographically, having just confirmed the doctrine of seven angels begotten of fasting. The lacuna content is irrecoverable; left untranslated.

Translated 'leader.' The form is most likely Greek παρα-ἀρχηγός 'co-leader / one-alongside-the-founder,' or possibly παράγωγος 'leader-aside, conductor, guide.' Mani is identifying himself as the apostolic leader/initiator of his church. The Greek prefix παρα- ('alongside') may emphasize his role as the appointed-by-side companion-figure of the cosmic powers, or as 'the secondary leader' under the Father. Cf. accumulated ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲏⲅⲟⲥ 'the leaders/chiefs' (without the παρα- prefix). The whole sentence asserts Mani's apostolic primacy: 'since I am the leader, while the fifty elect were with me in the church, while I was head over her.'

Translated as the Coptic numeral 'fifty' (= Sahidic ⲧⲁⲓⲟⲩ for 50), not as qualitative of ⲧⲁⲓⲟ 'honor'. The arithmetic confirms: 50 men × 3 Sundays × 7 angels = 1050 (line 11: ⲣ̄ⲙⲏⲧ ⲛ̄ϣⲉ ⲧⲁⲓⲟⲩ = 1000+50). Line 6 ϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛ̄ϣⲉ ⲧⲁⲓⲟⲩ = 350 = 50 × 7 angels per Sunday for all 50 men. The numerical reading makes the entire calculation coherent.

Rendered 'stood before me' from the Lycopolitan idiom: ⲡⲁⲙⲏⲧ = 'my midst, my presence' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' The opening situates the disciples standing in Mani's presence as he describes their fasting practice.
Translated as 1sg perfect of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand, establish' = 'I have established/stood (in).' The speaker reflects on the good they have stood/established through the three Sundays of fasting.
Lycopolitan reflexive ⲧⲕⲧⲁⲓ̈ = ⲕⲧⲟⲓ 'turn myself' + ⲁⲛ 'again.' Marks the transition from joyful arithmetic to grief — the speaker turns from reckoning blessings to confessing trouble.
Standard Coptic ⲧⲱⲃϩ̄ 'pray, entreat, beseech' with 2sg.m suffix. Marks the petitionary core of the disciple's address to Mani.

The disciple asks to be released from the πατρωνία 'patronage' of gods and angels — the cosmic-protective relationship pertaining to his ecclesiastical office (cf. ⲡⲁⲧⲣⲱⲛⲓⲁ in accumulated vocabulary). Rendered 'patronage of the gods and the angels' to preserve the technical Manichaean register.
Read as ⲧⲏⲧⲉ 'sum, total, completion' (variant of ⲧⲏ 'totality'). Fits the arithmetical context where the speaker is computing the grand total of angels begotten.

Translated as 'in your mouth, you yourself alone' — ⲣⲱⲕ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧⲕ is the standard Coptic emphatic-reflexive idiom (cf. ⲣⲱ⸗ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧ⸗) meaning 'thyself alone, by thy own self.' The leading [ⲍ] preposition specifies location: 'in your mouth' = i.e., the disciple's own utterance, contrasted with the truth itself. The Apostle is identifying the words as the disciple's private claim, not a teaching he has received from outside.

Translated 'which removes him from the suffering of the fasts.' The Lycopolitan ⲟⲩⲉⲓ̈ⲧϥ̄ likely combines ⲟⲩⲉⲓ 'be far/distant' (causative) + 3sg.m suffix = 'cause him to be far from.' The whole clause modifies ⲡⲉⲓ̈ 'this' (referring to the alleged 'nourishment'), reflecting the disciple's claim that some practice delivers from the suffering of fasting. Reading is moderate confidence; alternative readings (e.g., 'which they bring him') are possible but the 'remove from' sense fits best with following ⲛ̄ⲧⲗⲁⲓ̈ⲃⲉ 'from the suffering.'

Translated 'eager/willing' — qualitative of ⲣⲟⲟⲩⲧ 'be ready, prepared, joyful' (the standard Coptic verb of willingness/readiness). Modifies the 2sg subject in circumstantial: 'you being eager,' i.e., the disciple's eagerness in proclaiming his (mistaken) view.

Read ⲯⲱⲛⲉ as Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'turn aside, change' (with ⲯ for ⲡ in dialectal spelling), giving 'you did not turn aside from saying it.' Alternative: ⲯⲱⲛⲉ = ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'be sick, weary' giving 'you did not weary of saying it.' Both are contextually viable; chose 'turn aside' for stronger fit with the Apostle's accusation that the disciple boldly proclaimed his error.

Translated 'wasted' — apparent reduplicated qualitative of unidentified root, possibly cognate with ⲗⲁⲕⲗⲱⲕ 'soft, melt' (giving 'softened, weakened') or with a Lyc dialectal form for bodily decline. The triadic series 'wasted/sick/oppressed' marks progressive bodily failure; 'wasted' captures the cumulative-debilitation sense.

Read as Lyc reflex of ⲧⲁⲛϩⲟⲩⲧ 'entrust' + 2sg suffix = 'they have entrusted you.' With following ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to it,' yields 'the work to which you have been entrusted.' This is the same construction underlying English passive 'entrusted to (a task).'

Translated 'your body is holy unto you' — ⲁⲩⲟⲛ̄ here is the Lycopolitan existential predicate (cf. accumulated entry ⲁⲩⲟ̄ⲛ 'exists / there belongs to him'). The qualitative ⲉϩⲟⲩⲁⲭ = ⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ 'holy, pure' modifies ⲡⲉⲕⲥⲱⲙⲁ. The phrase belongs to what 'they shall say' to the disciple in the realm of rest — declaring that his bodily integrity has been preserved through fidelity to the work.

Translated 'harm' — lexeme of uncertain etymology, possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ϫⲃⲓⲛ 'lameness, deficiency' or related to ϭⲃⲃⲉ 'be weak.' Listed in the doublet/triplet with ⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'destruction' and ϯⲕⲉⲥ 'affliction' as the bodily ills from which the faithful disciple is preserved.

Translated 'this entire profit becomes worthless.' The form ⲛϯⲃⲁⲧ is obscure; tentatively read as ⲛ̄- (predicative/genitive) + ⲧⲃⲁⲧ from a root meaning 'spit, despise' (cf. Crum ⲧⲃⲏⲧ 'spittle/contempt'), yielding the predicate 'becomes-of-spittle' = 'becomes despised, becomes worthless.' Alternative readings (e.g., 'in vain,' 'lost') are possible. The argument requires the entire profit to be nullified if the work is refused.

Translated 'they do not give-heed-to ... the face of the profit.' Read ⲙⲁⲩⲧⲉ as Lycopolitan negative habitual ⲙⲁⲩ- + ⲧⲉ = 'they do not give' (the ⲧⲉ being a reduced infinitive of ϯ 'give'). With the restored object ⲡⲍⲟ ⲙ̄ⲡⲍⲏⲩ 'the face of the profit' (line 30), this yields the idiom ϯ-ϩⲟ ⲁ- 'give face/attention to,' standard Coptic for 'pay heed to, regard.' The Apostle's logic: even the wise (those most likely to grasp the truth) are not turning their face to the profit the disciple has been proclaiming, hence they will commit this sin (of refusal) along with him.

The lost word ending in -ⲓⲙⲟⲥ is most likely a Greek loanword. Plausible candidates include [ⲇⲟⲕ]ⲓⲙⲟⲥ 'approved, tested' (δόκιμος) or [ⲗⲟⲅ]ⲓⲙⲟⲥ 'reasonable, of repute' (λόγιμος). The sense 'wise men ... [approved/reasonable] who know the truth' fits the rhetorical structure but the specific term cannot be securely restored.

Translated 'this is the manner that I have' — the standard formulaic Apostle's self-assertion (cf. similar formulas elsewhere in the Kephalaia, e.g. K.193 'thus is the way'). The Apostle is contrasting his own constant teaching with the disciple's wavering. The sentence breaks at the page boundary; continuation would specify what 'I have' (taught/decreed/commanded).

Translated as 'the work' — Lyc ⲡⲣ̄- (article cluster) + ⲍⲱⲃ (= ϩⲱⲃ 'work,' already in glossary). The verbal idiom ⲣ̄-ⲡⲣ̄ⲍⲱⲃ 'do the work' is the controlling phrase of the kephalaion (also at lines 15, 22).

Translated tentatively as 'a portion / your portion.' The lexeme is unusual; appears here at line 3 as 'let a ⲍⲏⲣ become in your life' and at line 26 as 'your toil shall be reckoned to your ⲍⲏⲣ' — semantic field of 'share, account, recompense.' Possible Lyc reflex relating to ⲡⲱⲣⲱ 'lot' or a specific Manichaean technical term for the disciple's accumulated merit/account before the Apostle. Confidence moderate. Flagged for parallel attestations in subsequent kephalaia.

Translated as 'waver' based on context: line 4 'even though others ⲃⲁϣⲃⲉϣ' (others' negative behavior) parallels line 5 'do not ⲃⲁϣⲃⲉϣ' (warning to disciple). The reduplicated form likely related to ⲡⲱϣⲡⲱϣ 'split, divide' or a deficiency-verb yielding 'waver, be divided in heart, be lax.' Pairs with Greek παραιτεῖσθαι 'refuse, decline' as parallel negative behaviors to avoid. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Translated as 'refuse / decline' from Greek παραιτεῖσθαι 'beg off, decline, refuse.' The construction ⲡⲁⲣⲉⲧⲓ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϥ 'refuse himself' fits the moral exhortation: do not beg off from the work. Standard Greek loanword in Coptic.

Left as transliterated 'paraphon' — obscure Greek loanword in series ⲉⲁⲩ-ⲡⲟⲣⲟ-ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲫⲟⲛ ('glory-kingship-X') as honors of the proclaimer. Possible candidates: παρρησία 'boldness/free-speech' (corrupted spelling), παράφορον 'mark of distinction,' or παράκλησις 'exhortation.' Cannot identify with confidence; flagged for parallels.

Translated 'folds himself by himself, and turns himself by himself' — describing the brother of righteous heart who withdraws inward and remains alone. ⲁⲗϥ from ⲱⲗϥ̄ 'fold, bend' (cf. Crum); ⲕⲁⲧϥ̄ from ⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'turn.' The double ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉϥ 'alone' emphasizes solitary withdrawal — contrasted with the active proclamation that builds the Church.

'But the man himself who speaks, who commands' — pivot from the previous case (one who builds with his word and has no sin) to the contrasting case: the man who speaks and commands but does not himself do the work. The grammatical emphasis ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϥ 'himself' marks the personal accountability of the speaker.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲣⲍⲱⲃ ⲉϩⲁⲍⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲃⲉ
notes.decision: 'The work shall stand entirely upon him in the sin' — using the standard Coptic ⲱϩⲉ ⲉⲣⲁⲧ⸗ idiom 'stand on the feet of' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast'). The work-burden falls back upon the speaker who fails to act. ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲃⲉ likely Lyc article cluster + 'sin' rather than a possessive form.

'Your toil shall be reckoned to your portion' — using ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (in glossary) with directional ⲁ- 'to.' The construction parallels biblical-soteriological 'reckoning to one's account' (cf. Romans 4:3-5). The disciple's labor in church-building accrues to his ⲍⲏⲣ (portion/account/credit).

notes.coptic_form: ⲙⲁⲣⲉ ⲧⲉⲕⲟ̄ⲁⲙ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲉⲕⲉⲁⲩ ⲣ̄ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲉⲓ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈
notes.decision: 'Let your power and your glory help me' — standard disciple's petition closing the kephalaion. The disciple acknowledges that the proclaimer's work cannot succeed without the Apostle's continued power (ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ) and glory (ⲉⲁⲩ) standing behind him. ⲣ̄ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲉⲓ from Greek βοηθέω 'help, aid.'
